What if the hidden AI cost of your JavaScript framework is inflating your LLM spend? Nolan Lawson’s recent benchmark reveals that the same Opus 5.5 model can consume up to 30 % more tokens when using Next.js compared to SvelteKit for an identical small Pokémon‑search app.

The experiment measured four dimensions: wall‑clock development time, total tokens, lines of code, and Lighthouse performance and accessibility scores. Across multiple runs, token consumption showed high stochastic variance, sometimes doubling for the same framework, while Lighthouse metrics fluctuated enough to alter perceived speed rankings.

Beyond token counts, the benchmark found that stochastic LLM behavior can mask a framework’s raw runtime speed, and that performance scores like Largest Contentful Paint can swing between runs even with unchanged code.

“Framework choice matters when agents write code, not just when humans do.”  

Understanding these AI‑cost dimensions helps teams avoid hidden API expenses and choose tools that truly reduce token waste while maintaining quality.

The data reflects a single set of runs with Opus 5.5 on a small app; results may differ with other models or larger projects.

Which metric would you start tracking to manage AI‑assisted development costs?  

Full breakdown with sources: https://buildwithsaksham.in/blog/the-hidden-ai-cost-of-javascript-frameworks
